ui._comment_sessionTitle: v2.1.33 (Issue #77): opt-in. bkit no longer names your session by default. Set enabled=true to have bkit label the session with the active PDCA feature and phase; even then it never overwrites a title you set with --name or /rename.

pdca._comment_staleDays: v2.1.36 (ENH-453): lib/pdca/lifecycle.js read `pdca.automation.staleDays`, a section this file has never had, so the shipped value could never take effect. The reader now matches this key.

sprint._comment: v2.1.13 Sprint Management defaults (DEEP-6). Per-sprint overrides via sprint.config.{...} at sprint init time take precedence.

contextSizing._comment_minSprints: v2.1.36 (ENH-458): RESERVED, NOT CONSUMED. context-sizer.js merges this key (:171) but nothing reads cfg.minSprints; only maxSprints is enforced (:321). A floor on the sprint count has no specified behaviour, so it is declared rather than given an invented one.

promptCaching1h._comment_ccMinVersion: v2.1.36 (ENH-456): `ccMinVersion` was removed. It restated the floor already held by FEATURE_VERSION_MAP.promptCaching1h in lib/infra/cc-version-checker.js, in a different format ('v2.1.108' vs '2.1.108'), and nothing read it. Two places to state one version is a drift waiting to happen; the checker is the single source.
promptCaching1h.note: Set ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1 in shell before launching CC for 30-40% token savings on long PDCA sessions. ENH-265 (bkit v2.1.9).

_comment_permissions: v2.1.36 (ENH-458): DECLARATIVE. This block is the safe-default policy bkit RECOMMENDS, in Claude Code's permission-rule syntax so it can be copied into .claude/settings.json. bkit does not enforce it and Claude Code does not read this file, so editing it changes nothing on its own. Enforcement of destructive shapes lives in lib/control/destructive-detector.js (16 rules), not here. test/controllable-ai/safe-defaults.test.js asserts these values — note that this checks the recommendation's content, not that anything enforces it.

automation._comment_maxConcurrentFeatures: v2.1.36 (ENH-458): DUPLICATE, NOT CONSUMED. The live setting is `multiFeature.maxActiveFeatures` (read at lib/core/config.js:136). Two keys for one concept is how a value gets edited in the wrong place; use multiFeature.maxActiveFeatures.
automation._comment_gateTimeoutMs: v2.1.36 (ENH-458): RESERVED, NOT CONSUMED. No gate evaluation path is time-bounded today.
automation._comment_emergency: v2.1.36 (ENH-453): emergencyStopEnabled shipped here and nothing read it, while automation-controller.js read emergencyFallbackLevel, which was never shipped. Both halves of one feature were disconnected from the file that claims to configure them. Both are now wired.

guardrails._comment_destructiveDetection: v2.1.36 (ENH-458): DECLARATIVE, NOT A SWITCH. The Destructive Detector cannot be turned off at runtime, and that is deliberate: test/security/integrity-verification.test.js IV-09 asserts detect() ignores the _disabled flag precisely so a guard cannot be neutralised from inside a session. Setting this to false does NOT disable detection. It is kept as a declaration of intent and as the anchor for that contract; wiring it to a real off-switch would overturn IV-09 and is a maintainer decision, not a config edit. False-positive relief comes from rule precision (see the 12->1 measurement in this release), not from an off-switch.
guardrails._comment_blastRadiusLimit: v2.1.36 (ENH-458): RESERVED, NOT CONSUMED. lib/control/blast-radius.js grades a change set and reports a level; it has no configurable ceiling, so there is no place for this value to act. Wiring it would mean inventing a policy nobody has specified. Recorded here rather than silently ignored.
guardrails._comment_checkpointOnDestructive: v2.1.36 (ENH-458): RESERVED, NOT CONSUMED. A destructive command is denied or asked at PreToolUse, not checkpointed — and bkit never observes the user's answer to an ask, so there is no point at which 'before the destructive operation proceeds' can be detected. Left declared, not wired.

quality._comment_unwired: v2.1.36 (ENH-458): gateEnabled, metricsCollection and historyMaxDataPoints are RESERVED, NOT CONSUMED. Quality gates are evaluated unconditionally by lib/application/sprint-lifecycle/quality-gates.js evaluateGate(); metrics collection and history retention have no configurable path today. `thresholds` and `regressionGuard` ARE read. These three are recorded as declarative so the file no longer implies control it does not have.
